messages:
sasha: Kicking off quick perf/NET warmup for nyc2 GPU pool. Goal: smoke throughput + end-to-end p95 checks before handing to SRE for soak. Running kernel/driver sanity + MTU/TC/ebpf checks. Will post results.
alex: Thanks — do we already have the driver/kernel matrix for nyc2 nodes? want to confirm no mismatch with AMI baseline.
jon: Nodes are on ubuntu-22.04 + nvidia-driver 535.86.05, docker runtime runc 1.1.4, kernels 6.1.53. I ran dkms compile locally, no errors.
maria: Starting a short-scale perf run on one node (4xA100 40G). Test plan: 10 warmup runs, then 5 x 1-min steady-state runs with loadgen (concurrency 16, seq len 512). Posting command:

```
./loadgen --model gpt-8b-qat --concurrency 16 --seq 512 --duration 60 --batching continuous
```

maria: Also running netprobe to validate path MTU and link saturations:

```
sudo iperf3 -c bench-proxy.internal -P 8 -t 30 -M 9000
```

sasha: Good. Pay attention to NIC drop counters and softirq spikes. If p95 > 180ms we investigate kernel preemption/irqbalance.
kevin: Quick note — cross-rack BGP session to spine-2 had a flapped route this morning. Might affect east-west tail latency briefly. I cleared the session and pulled logs; no persistent drops now.
alex: On the driver side, we saw an NVLink firmware mismatch on previous build. Can we run this snippet on all nodes to confirm nvlink health?

```
nvlink-status.sh || true
/opt/nvidia/bin/nvlink_query --status
```

jon: Ran nvlink check on node-03: all links UP, 100% lanes. No errors in dmesg besides benign "GPU reset completed" from earlier boot.
maria: First steady-state run metrics (node-03):
- median latency: 42ms
- p95 latency: 128ms
- tokens/sec: 9.1k
- GPU util: 91% (overall), memory alloc stable
- kernel sycalls p95: 3.4ms

maria: I also saw TCP retransmits ~120 in 1-min window on one run. correlating with a small interrupt storm at 11:12:23.
sasha: Which NIC? please capture ethtool stats and irq mapping for that interface. use:

```
ETHTOOL_IF=ens5
sudo ethtool -S $ETHTOOL_IF | egrep "rx_errors|tx_errors|rx_no_buf"
cat /proc/interrupts | egrep $(basename /sys/class/net/$ETHTOOL_IF/device/irq)
```

alex: FYI, MTU across the node-subnet is 9000, but some leaf switches were on 1500 earlier — I pushed a config to standardize. Might cause small fragmentation until flows age out.
infra-bot: perf-check-runner: job 4821 completed for nyc2/node-03. Summary: PASS (smoke) — but WARN: intermittent tcp_retransmits. Artifacts: s3://redwood-perf/nyc2/4821/
jon: Let's rerun perf with packet_capture for 30s overlapping the spike window. Use tcpdump -w to s3 via sidecar.
maria: Rerun #2 in 3m with tcpdump sidecar. Also enabling kernel rcpu_balance toggle (set to 0) to see if softirq pins change.
kevin: I patched the BGP timers on spine-2 to be more conservative; will monitor for any session flaps for next hour.
sasha: Good plan. If second run still shows retransmits, escalate to network team with pcap + ethtool stats. If latency p95 increases >200ms on steady runs, revert to smaller batch sizes and flag for model-variant fallback.
alex: One more ops-cost note — nyc2 dedicated capacity has higher egress cost. For long soak, consider routing eval traffic through cheaper region mirror for non-production traffic to save ~$2k/mo.
jon: Logged next steps in run 4822 artifact. tagging @networking-team and @oncall for handoff when soak is green.
maria: Final quick paste of run #2 steady-state summary (after MTU fix): median 40ms, p95 115ms, tokens/sec 9.3k, tcp retransmits <5. Marking smoke as resolved. Moving to soak queue.
sasha: Thanks everyone. Handoff checklist updated in run artifact. Leaving this thread for SRE handoff. :thumbsup:
